The damned bull was catching flies, his mouth gaping open and drooling against Mydei’s breasts, as if he were trying to lap up more milk in his sleep. Mydei had to roll his eyes. How many times had Phainon came? Best in show and he couldn’t even handle cuming inside a heifer a few times.

Mydei blinked down at the stretch in his abdomen where the bull’s cock remained, before weaving his own hands into Phainon’s. He smiled to himself. As he drifted to sleep, he wondered…

Who would their calf take after more?

Mydei pouted in his sleep.

He was going to have the stronger genes, obviously. No way Phainon was winning that one.

 

A bit later Mydei’s farmer – accompanied by Phainon’s own farmer – came to check on them. They were quite surprised to open the barn doors, only to see their two prize hybrids had finally decided to fornicate and leave their mess everywhere. The two hybrids hadn’t even bothered to try and get any milk into a bucket. Most of it stuck to their joined chests – the rest was drying around Phainon’s mouth.

Though the two farmers were relieved to see their hybrids had finally copulated, it wasn’t exactly at the most ideal of times. Phainon’s farmer had travelled all the way from Aedes Elysiae to collect him – a journey that took several days and nights by foot. Since the two hybrids were now getting along as intended, it would have been ideal to leave them to continue their…activities for another week, to make sure their love making was successful. However, it was such a trip, Phainon’s farmer couldn’t make the trip back without his bull. Not to mention, Mydei’s farmer had already found a new bull, and it was clear the two bulls didn’t get along and couldn’t coexist. There was also the issue of Phainon needing to return to his home for winter. He was the sole bull of the remote mountain village and he did a lot to keep the isolated village safe from wolves and other threats over winter. No matter how much the two hybrids seemed to be getting along, Phainon needed to return home.

Both hybrids understood this. And later that day, Mydei found himself standing by the gate, clutching his hands together as he watched Phainon load the cart for his farmer. Phainon was then buckled into the harness, ready for his long journey home.

Phainon had made a good recovery from their morning activities. There was a spring in his step and sparkles in his crystal blue eyes. A few noticeable bruises dotted his toned, and long scratch marks weaved their way down his chest and back. Those didn’t seem to bother the bull at all. If anything, he was proud to show them off in front of the farmers, a token of his successful work.

Mydei hadn’t come off their session quite as well. He was wobbly on his feet, and had to lean against the gate just to keep himself upright, lest his legs give away completely. He was beginning to think that maybe he should’ve zonked out and slept like a baby, just like how Phainon had slept on his chest. However, if he had done so, then he wouldn’t have been able to admire the sleeping bull, weaving fingers through silky silver hair, ingrained the feeling of the two of them pressed together into his mind forever.  

There were purple hickeys on his neck and shoulders, but mostly at his breasts – of which his tiny bikini top did little to cover. It was quite embarrassing to face his farmer with a purpling bruise right between his tits. That being said, his tits felt a lot lighter after being drained of milk, and there was no more fire of heat raging through his body. Instead, he felt a gentle afterglow. Or as Phainon had said, that was his mark on the cow, a sign that Mydei belonged to him now.

The two hybrids faced each other. Mydei squeezed a hand at his chest, trying to swallow back the sudden surge of emotion that overcame him. He didn’t quite understand what he was feeling. Never had he looked at a bull – looked at Phainon out of all bulls – and felt the urge to cry on the spot. He blamed it on the sex. Phainon had exported some of his pathetic puppiness into him whilst they fucked. That could be the only explanation.

He wasn’t going to miss the bull. The fiend who had bugged him like a hungry mosquito. Absolutely not. Mydei would have his old life back as soon as the bull stepped down the trail.

Only, that wasn’t true. Mydei couldn’t even pretend that was true. Especially when Phainon smiled down at him so fondly.

“I’m so happy I got to be the bull to breed you, Mydei,” Phainon smiled, as if that sentence wasn’t hideously embarrassing for the heifer. 

“You really still call yourself a breeding bull?” Mydei scoffed. “You bred a single cow once and then called it a day. What kind of bull does that?” Perhaps if he joked and teased the bull, he could pretend this was just another normal interaction between them.

“I hate to agree with you, but maybe you’re right,” Phainon sighed. “Being a breeding bull isn’t for me. That would require me to breed more than one cow.” Phainon stepped forward. A smug smile appeared on his face. “And I only have eyes for one.”

“HKS,” Mydei rolled his eyes, though he couldn’t help the strawberry milk blush that foamed his cheeks in a cute pink glow.

“Don’t you go getting near that cliff again,” Phainon mused, ruffling a hand through Mydei’s blond hair. Mydei leaned into the touch, his tail swishing behind him.

“You don’t need to protect me,” he said. He tried to sound grumpy, but in truth he was butting his head into Phainon’s hand, seeking out the buzz of Phainon’s calloused touch against his scalp. Phainon chuckled and scratched right behind Mydei’s floppy ear, making the heifer sigh contently.

“Maybe not,” Phainon said. He reached down until he was smoothing a hand over Mydei’s lower chest. “But it’s not just you that you’re caring for now.”

Mydei sucked in a breath between his teeth. He looked at his chest. He sighed when Phainon squeezed his hand against the soft flesh slightly.

“I wish I could see you filling out, growing round,” Phainon whispered. “You’d look so cute, all plump and soft.” A sadness caught in the bull’s eyes as he drew away.

Mydei looked up at him. The sun was setting behind the bull. Phainon’s farmer was watching them, waiting for them to say their goodbyes.

Mydei didn’t want to say goodbye. He wanted Phainon to stay. He wanted Phainon to breed and milk him every day. He wanted Phainon to throw him compliments as his body grew smoother and round to hold their calf. He wanted Phainon to curl against him in the straw on cold winter nights. Wanted to wake in his embrace and take morning walks with him in the fresh spring air whilst they waited together for the day their calf would be born amongst the spring blossoms.

Phainon had to go home. He knew that. However…

“Will I see you again?” Mydei asked quietly, searching deeply in Phainon’s eyes for the answer he desired.

Phainon was caught off-guard by the emotion in Mydei’s voice. He cupped the heifer’s cheek in his large hand, pressing a kiss to his lips.

“You will. I promise. I’ll find my way back to you.”

 “Then I’ll be waiting.” Mydei nuzzled into his hand, kissing him back.  “Don’t forget, Deliverer.”

“Forget you?” The bull scoffed, eyes shining. “Like I’d ever.”

Mydei wrapped his arms around himself as he watched Phainon leave into the sunset. It already felt cold without the bull at his side.

Phainon turned back a final time and sent him one last wink.

Mydei huffed; a tremble in his lips turning into a smile.

It was okay; Phainon leaving. He knew they would meet again.

I never miss.

Mydei clutched his chest tighter.

After all, Phainon’s mark remained with him no matter how far away the bull travelled.

 

*

 

Mydei stepped into the show ring. An audience wrapped around the ring, examining how he composed himself, the gait of his walk, how good his body was. Mydei paid his audience no attention, he was fixated on only one thing, and that was the tiny calf bundled in blankets, wrapped close in his arms, which he attempted to conceal from the prying eyes watching them around the ring.

The bidding went back and forth. It was the longest session so far, several vying to bid on him. After all, no one could remember the last time a pure-blooded Kremnoan cow was put up for auction. The price was bound to rise, tension thick as butter.

Finally, the hammer fell. The winning bidder raised their panel, the auctioneer noting it down. Number 33. That was the winning bidder’s number.

Mydei was led out of the ring by his farmer. He couldn’t have felt more relieved, yet more daunted at the same time. He hated being in that ring, so many pairs of eyes on him and his calf. But now it was over, and so was his time with his farmer.

He’d found out that his farmer intended to sell him just a few days ago. It felt sporadic, Mydei couldn’t understand why his farmer wanted to part with him so suddenly. Mydei had grown up on that farm since he was just a young calf, he could barely remember a life before living there. His farmer had never been particularly sympathetic, but he was safe, familiar.

Now, Mydei had no idea who would be his farmer, or where he would be going.

Mydei heard a tiny cry and looked down. His tiny calf, just a week old, was bundled in blankets against his chest. She had just woken up, unaware of what was going on around her. She could only gaze up at her mother, letting out little babbles and cries.

His farmer had wanted to keep her and sell Mydei on, but Mydei had so fiercely put up a fight that he had agreed to sell them as a pair. He refused to go anywhere without her, keeping her pressed securely against his chest at all times. She was so small, smaller than most newborn calves and she easily got cold. No one else understood her or what she needed except Mydei. He had already memorised her every cry. He knew when she was tired, when she wanted milk, when she just wanted to feel her mother’s warm kisses blown across her tummy.

Mydei was led into a holding pen at the side of the auction ring. His farmer tied the lead rope in place, patting his shoulder before heading off to fill out some more paperwork with the lucky bidder who had just won the auction. Around Mydei, the buzz of the auction continued. He could hear the overhead commentator, describing the next hybrid that had gone up for auction to the crowd.

Mydei zoned everything out, concentrating on his little calf. It wasn’t just because she was his baby, but she was the most beautiful calf Mydei had ever seen. Opaline sparkling eyes, bright and blue like the sky was blinking up at him. A pair of cute little white ears, paired with a tiny white tail. Just starting to grow on the top of her head, the first specs of pointy silver hair. A little bit at the top of her head had already grown longer than the rest, and was already curling slightly to form a springy piggy-tail ahoge.  

She looked so much like her father already.

She was reaching her tiny hands out toward him. She was babbling, smiling away, just happy to see her mother in her little world.

Looking at her tore Mydei apart. Tears welled in his eyes. He wanted to protect her, keep her safe, give her the best life he possibly could. But now he had no idea what was going to happen to them. He was scared. Scared that he’d fail her. Scared someone would try and separate them. He was scared that he wasn’t enough to keep her safe on his own.

Mydei lifted her high, nuzzling their noses together as he hugged her close. No matter what, he was determined to keep his calf with him. He’d forfeit everything he had to keep her safe.

He placed a kiss on her forehead and she giggled, petting his cheeks with her tiny chubby hands. Mydei swallowed back his tears, kissing her softly.

Mydei heard footsteps approaching them and his shoulders rose. He wrapped the baby closer to his chest instinctively.

But then he caught the scent. Fresh wheat fields, free mountain air, and musk. A scent unmistakable to him.

Mydei turned around, his eyes going wide.

“I thought I’d find you here,” the bull smirked, even though his sky blue eyes were already spotty with tears.

The same silver hair, a curly ahoge sprouting from top that couldn’t be weeded no matter how hard anyone tried to remove it. Those large horns reaching up to the gods. And that smile. A spitting image of the baby held tenderly in Mydei’s arms.

They hadn’t seen each other for nine months. But there he was. The father of his newborn calf.

“…Phainon?” Mydei shook his head, almost in disbelief. He went to surge forward towards the bull, only to be prevented by the lead rope which tied him in place. His calf made a gurgling noise, sensing a shift in her mother’s emotions.

Phainon smiled wider, running up to him. They came together, nuzzling each other’s noses and hair. Mydei shuddered as he tried not to cry. The bull’s scent washed over him, lips peppering kisses across the bridge of his nose, washing away his worries so easily. Mydei breathed a sigh of relief, one he wasn’t sure how long he’d been holding. Maybe he’d been holding it ever since he watched Phainon’s silhouette fade over the hills the last time they saw each other nine months ago.

“You’re finally here,” Mydei breathed.

“I told you I wouldn’t forget,” Phainon hummed against his skin. “Not ever.”

Phainon looked down and his eyes went wide. He gazed down at the tiny thing bundled in Mydei’s arms. The little calf that shared his silver hair and white markings, who looked up at the two of them with beautiful blue eyes, as blue as the sky on a cloudless summer day.

The bull’s breath left him completely. Mydei heard him wheeze. “Is that…?”

Mydei smiled. “She’s all yours,” he said. “…Ours.” He nudged the bundle against Phainon’s chest, prompting him to hold her. The bull did, taking her oh so gently. He cradled her like she weighed nothing. His shoulders shook. The bull bit his lip to restrain a whimper. “I’m sorry…she’s so small,” Mydei said, his ears drooping. Phainon’s eyes immediately went wide, looking at the cow in shock.

“What? N-no don’t be sorry! You have absolutely nothing to be sorry for.” Phainon looked back down at their calf. He gently squeezed her cheeks. “…She’s so beautiful Dei,” he shuddered. “You did such a good job baby.”

Mydei’s ears perked at the praise from his bull. He nudged Phainon’s side. “You’re not just saying that because she looks just like you?”

“Well, that is a bonus,” Phainon took a steadying breath. “She’s perfect, Dei. So fucking perfect.”

Mydei observed the bull cradling his baby and his heart swelled to a height he didn’t think possible. He’d always prided himself on being reserved with his emotions. Maybe it was his new motherly instincts, but the sight in front of him was doing unspeakable things to his insides. He wanted to laugh, to sob, to blabber to Phainon about every little thing their calf had done since she’d been born. All her little mannerisms and what each tiny moo meant, fill him in on everything he’d missed.

Instead, he stood quietly, content to be an observer in this moment between father and daughter. Bulls didn’t usually deal with their offspring. Breeding bulls were sent to breed entire herds. As such, calves born the following year often all had the same father. Some bulls fathered so many calves that they couldn’t possibly be deeply connected with each one, and instead settled for watching over the entire herd. Other bulls would’ve long moved on to the next herd by the time his first herd had bared his calves.

To see a bull cradling a single tiny calf like the moment was sacred – was not a sight often seen. Phainon wasn’t a normal bull though. He had spent months pursuing a single cow, and then never pursued another. Besides, Mydei wouldn’t have let any old bull get him pregnant. He would have only ever chosen this odd HKS to be the father of his child, and no one else.

“Hey there little princess,” Phainon cooed to his baby. “Aren’t you the most beautiful thing ever?” Phainon kissed his baby on the forehead. “Don’t you worry darling, daddy’s here.” The tiny calf responded with a chirpy sound. She reached up a little hand, patting the bull on the cheek. “Look baby, I think she likes me.” Phainon said proudly as he kissed the calf’s tiny hand.

“Well, you are her father,” Mydei smiled. He came a little closer, so that the baby was between both their chests. “I had her exactly a week ago today,” he said.

“A week?” Phainon repeated. “I wish I could’ve seen her from the very start, but at least I’m here now. I wouldn’t want to miss a moment longer with either of you.”

Mydei’s smile fell. Sensing it, Phainon handed the calf back to Mydei. Mydei looked down at her.

“Our farmer just sold us at auction,” Mydei admitted. He shook his head. “I don’t know who the winning bidder was.” Mydei clutched his calf tightly.  “This new farm might take us a long way away, maybe even further than before…I don’t know what’s going to happen to us.”

Phainon watched the pair of them quietly. He put a hand on Mydei’s shoulder. When Mydei didn’t look up, he cleared his throat. That prompted Mydei to look at him. Phainon had an unusual expression on his face. His lips drawn in a thin line but his eyes dancing about, struggling to conceal the rampant emotions beneath.

Phainon held up a small panel of wood. On the panel was a number painted in black paint.

Number 33.

Mydei didn’t understand what it meant straight away. It was only when Phainon cocked his head and smiled that he realised.

“You’re both coming home with me,” Phainon said. Mydei suddenly felt dizzy. He was glad Phainon was there to support him.

“H-how did you? The money –” Mydei stammered. Phainon wrapped his other arm beneath the blankets that held his calf.

“You don’t need to worry about the money, or anything else,” Phainon said. He nuzzled close, kissing Mydei’s forehead. “My farmer is filling in the paperwork as we speak. The cart is already prepared. I spent all winter building us a barn at home. Everything is sorted out. We just need the final thing.” He tapped Mydei on the nose. “And that’s my two beautiful princesses.”

Mydei was completely speechless. All that worrying. Carrying their baby on his own for months. The fear of not being able to provide for her, to keep her safe.

And here he was, swooping in to save them both with that stupid smile on his face. He’d been planning to do so all this time.

“Deliverer…” He breathed. “Phainon!” Mydei buried his face in the bull’s chest to cover his tears. The bull’s arms went around him, their baby placed protectively between their bodies.

Phainon stroked his hands through Mydei’s blond hair. It had grown longer over the winter, but still just as pretty and soft as ever.

“You’ve done so good baby,” he murmured into his ear, pressing a kiss to the fluffy lobe. “But you don’t have to do it alone anymore. I’m here…I’m here.”

Their lips met. Mydei kissed his bull deeply. He considered trying to choke himself in those kisses. Maybe then he’d wake up and find out this wasn’t real. But then Phainon’s tail was wrapping around his own and Mydei was gasping into their kiss. Between them, their calf gurgled loudly. Mydei knew that sound. She was excited, thrilled even.

Phainon pulled back only to undo the lead rope that tied Mydei in place, then he was smiling widely and joining their mouths together again. He used his lips to force Mydei to smile, and Mydei gladly let him, finally relaxing into the kiss.

 

A bit later, Phainon led the way to the small cart prepared for them. Their ride home. Mydei bid farewell to his farmer with a courteous bow. His farmer nodded back at him, wishing him well. Then Phainon took his hand. The bull kissed his knuckles, bowing low.

“Princesses, take your seats,” he said. He smiled fondly. “Let’s go home.”

Phainon helped Mydei get into the cart. He helped rearrange the straw that had been placed inside, making sure mother and calf were comfortably sat. The little calf had fallen asleep. Phainon promised a smooth journey home. “I’ll get us home in style,” he promised. “She’ll sleep like a hibernating bear. But do let me know when she wants to be fed and I’ll stop us.”

“How courteous of you,” Mydei responded.

“Wouldn’t want all that milk to go down the wrong way,” Phainon responded, His eyes flashed darkly. “Also, I want to see her suckling on your tits.”

Mydei scowled at him, but only for a moment. This bull. He never changed. Fortunately for him, Mydei didn’t either. He couldn’t stop himself from smiling despite the bull’s filthy words – and no doubt filthier thoughts.

Phainon kneeled down beside Mydei, coming next to his ear. His voice suddenly went low, his bright demeanour dissipating. “When we get home…gonna put another one in you.”

Mydei shivered. Phainon had already returned to his innocently sunny self as if nothing had happened between the two of them.

Two could play at that game.

Before Phainon could pull away, Mydei grabbed him by a horn. Phainon let out a surprised noise as Mydei brought him down, their faces level.

“…Only one?” Mydei questioned coyly, an eyebrow raised and a twinkle in his eye.

Phainon was quickly scrambling to clear his throat, his cheeks going as red as the twilight settling above their heads. His smile was wide and beaming, however.

“Is that a challenge?” Phainon asked. He kissed the forehead of their calf. “You remember I said I never miss, right?” The bull then leaned in to kiss Mydei, all teeth and smiles.

“Perhaps…I’ve forgotten,” Mydei lied, licking the bull’s lips with his tongue, a playful swish of his blond tail.

Phainon smirked against his lips. “Well then, challenge accepted.”

 

End.
